# A status page your SaaS customers actually trust

Monitor every dependency, open incidents automatically, and show customers a branded status page on your own subdomain, without standing up a status tool of your own.

## Monitor the whole stack

Your API, your database, your payment provider, your mail sender. A SaaS is down whenever any dependency your customers feel is down, so each one gets its own monitor: HTTP, TCP, DNS, TLS, domain, ping, heartbeat and browser-flow checks every 60 seconds, each with its own expectations and its own alert channels. A slow TLS handshake on the payments endpoint and a broken DNS record on the docs site are different problems, and they can page different people.

## Tell customers before they tell you

A down monitor opens an incident automatically and posts it to your public page, so the page updates before the first support ticket lands. Add a human note when you know more and your customers watch the fix land in real time. Subscribers get every update by confirmed email or signed webhook, which means the people who care most stop refreshing the page and stop writing to support.
